import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot showing the survival rate by Pclass, separated by Sex
# The 'kind="bar"' in catplot by default calculates the mean of the y-variable (survived)

g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='pclass',
    y='survived',
    col='sex',
    kind='bar',
    errorbar=None, # Remove error bars for cleaner visualization of means
    palette='viridis',
    height=5,
    aspect=0.9
)

# Set titles and labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Rate")
g.set_titles("Survival Rate by {col_name}")
g.fig.suptitle("Titanic Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex", y=1.03, fontsize=16) # Adjust y to prevent overlap

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot showing the survival rate by Pclass, separated by Sex
# The 'kind="bar"' in catplot by default calculates the mean of the y-variable (survived)
# for each category, which represents the survival rate.
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='pclass',
    y='survived',
    col='sex',
    kind='bar',
    errorbar=None, # Remove error bars for cleaner visualization of means
    palette='viridis',
    height=5,
    aspect=0.9
)

# Set titles and labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Rate")
g.set_titles("Survival Rate by {col_name}")
g.fig.suptitle("Titanic Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex", y=1.03, fontsize=16) # Adjust y to prevent overlap
